summary: Uneven GPU-credit depletion in dedicated pool causing autoscaler under-provisioning and noisy-tenant spillover
description: Issue summary: VertexCart reports repeated midday throughput collapses from their dedicated pool over the last 48 hours. Impact: p50 stable but p95/p99 token throughput drops by 60-80% for 5-20 minute windows, causing user-facing latency spikes and queued request backpressure. Environment: production dedicated pool (vertexcart-reserved-3), region us-east-1, model gptj-6b-8k-quant. Initial symptom: autoscaler did not add capacity during sustained long-lived chat streams that heavily used KV cache and kept GPU credit counters low for certain GPUs, triggering scheduler to leave those GPUs out of allocation despite logical free slots, resulting in uneven capacity and noisy-tenant spillover.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Recreate customer workload: 800 concurrent long-lived streaming sessions with 30-60 token pings every 8-12s using pinned model gptj-6b-8k-quant
2) Enable KV cache reuse (context pinning) to simulate real VertexCart traffic patterns
3) Observe allocator GPU-credit metrics and scheduler assignment for pool vertexcart-reserved-3
4) Watch autoscaler decision logs during sustained 10-20 minute window of uneven per-GPU credit depletion
observed_behavior: Autoscaler scaled only 1 additional shard when 3 were required; scale decision delayed ~2m after p95 latency rose
GPU credit counter showed drop-to-zero on 2 of 6 GPUs in the pool while remaining GPUs retained higher credit — scheduler avoided zero-credit GPUs for new attachments
Traffic from other tenants (noisy short-stream tenant) spiked and occupied reclaimed slots, causing VertexCart queues to lengthen
Console traces show many small streams preempting batch slots and triggering slot fragmentation
expected_behavior: Autoscaler should detect aggregate queueing and user-visible latency SLO violations and proactively add capacity; scheduler should prefer balanced attachments and not permanently avoid GPUs with transient low credit once they recover
logs_and_metrics: Kibana query: service:autoscaler AND pool:vertexcart-reserved-3 AND level:WARN
customer_impact: VertexCart reported checkout latency regressions impacting 12k end-users during afternoon peak; they temporarily routed some traffic to fallback hosted model which increased per-token cost and degraded content quality
investigation_notes: 03/12 13:30 - Support received initial bug report from VertexCart (CS) describing repeated 10-20 minute p99 spikes.
03/12 14:00 - SRE (Priya Kapoor) started correlation: identified GPU credit depletion counter on subset of GPUs in pool vertexcart-reserved-3.

03/12 15:10 - Hypothesis A: long-lived KV-cache heavy streams charge a different 'credit' weight causing uneven battery-style drain across GPUs. Evidence: credit drain aligns with long-session counts per GPU node.

03/12 16:05 - Hypothesis B: scheduler affinity kept older attachments pinned to same GPUs; when those GPUs dipped in credit they were excluded from future attachments leading to fragmentation and under-utilization. Evidence: scheduler logs show repeated 'skip-gpu low-credit' entries for gpu_id 3 and 5.

03/13 09:20 - Observed noisy-tenant short streams (tenant id noisy-payments) started bursty attach/disconnects coincident with VertexCart p99 spikes; short streams consumed newly freed slots and prevented rebalancing.
03/13 11:00 - Reproduced locally with scaled-down workload; autoscaler thresholds rely on avg_cpu/queue_length but not per-gpu credit distribution, leading to delayed scale-ups.

03/14 08:40 - Engineering experiment: temporarily disabled per-gpu credit avoidance in scheduler for pool vertexcart-reserved-3; immediate improvement in p95/p99 for 6 minutes but noisy tenant still caused quick re-fragmentation.
comments: Ava Martin (Support) 2026-03-12: Customer reports recurring throughput collapses during midday. Attached their request trace and example session IDs.

Priya Kapoor (SRE) 2026-03-12: Found gpu_credit=0 on two GPUs. Opening allocator traces; suspect KV-cache long-lived sessions weight differently. Assigning to Diego for follow-up on scheduler behavior.

Diego Chen (Assignee) 2026-03-13: Running targeted repro and will instrument per-gpu attach histograms. Plan: add temporary rule to allow re-attaching to GPUs with low credit after X seconds, and tune autoscaler to consider per-gpu credit imbalance as an early signal.
VertexCart (Customer) 2026-03-13: Thanks — we can provide a controlled window to replay traffic. Major impact to checkout latency; appreciate ETA on mitigation.

Diego Chen 2026-03-14: Deployed temporary scheduler change to pool (allow-recovering-gpus=true) at 2026-03-14T07:30Z. Early telemetry shows p99 improvement to pre-incident baseline for 18m windows. Working on permanent fix and autoscaler enhancement.
Support (Ava) 2026-03-14: Customer confirmed reduced errors after temporary mitigation; will keep in monitoring and coordinate change freeze for permanent rollout.
action_items: Short-term: Keep allow-recovering-gpus flag enabled for vertexcart-reserved-3 for 48h and monitor p95/p99 (owner: Diego)
Short-term: Throttle noisy short-stream tenant during VertexCart peak window as stop-gap (owner: CS/SRE)
Medium-term: Autoscaler enhancement to consume per-gpu credit distribution as an input signal (owner: autoscaler team, PR referenced)
Medium-term: Scheduler improvement to prefer balanced attach distribution and to include transient low-credit re-attach policy (owner: scheduler team)
Follow-up: Postmortem and runbook update documenting GPU-credit phenomenon and mitigations (owner: SRE/Docs)
Customer follow-up: Schedule a 1:1 with VertexCart to review mitigation and confirm traffic replay window (owner: CS)
resolution: In progress - temporary scheduler flag deployed and customer reported immediate improvement. Root cause likely interaction of per-gpu credit accounting + long-lived KV-cache-heavy sessions + noisy short-stream tenant occupying freed slots. Engineering to implement permanent autoscaler and scheduler fixes; postmortem scheduled after 72h observation window.
resolution_notes: Temporary mitigation: allow-recovering-gpus=true toggled on 2026-03-14T07:30Z for pool vertexcart-reserved-3. Observed p99 drop back to baseline for multiple recovery windows.
Workaround used by customer: route a fraction (10%) of traffic to hosted fallback for 3 hours during the worst window to reduce tail latency while we stabilize.
Planned permanent fix: autoscaler change to include per-gpu credit skew metric and scheduler change to rebalance attachments proactively; ETA for rollout: 2026-03-28.
